column1: # What go-pfcp v0.0.24 reads otherwise than the crate, in the corpus of the test go_pfcp: the
# aspect, the IE type (`message`, `*` for any, or `>=N` for N and above), what the crate
# reads, what go-pfcp reads, the clause of TS 29.244 V19.6.0, the side that the clause
# supports (crate, go-pfcp, both or neither), and why. tests/go_pfcp.rs says what each

column7: A vendor IE has a Length below the two octets of its Enterprise ID: the crate keeps it as octets and check() tells it; go-pfcp refuses the message
An IE does not frame within a grouped IE: the crate keeps that grouped IE as octets, decodes the message and check() tells the IE Invalid length; go-pfcp refuses the message
An IE of the message does not frame: go-pfcp takes an IE header with no octets after it whatever its Length, and reads the octets after the Message Length as IEs
The Message Length is not the length of the octets after the first four: go-pfcp does not read the Message Length

column4: stops after a grouped IE whose IEs do not frame
column7: go-pfcp refuses a scope whose grouped IE does not frame its IEs; the crate keeps that grouped IE as octets, check() tells it Invalid length, and the crate reads the IEs after it

column4: stops at a vendor IE too short for its Enterprise ID
column7: A vendor IE has its Enterprise ID after its Length: go-pfcp refuses the scope; the crate frames the IE without one, and check() tells it

column3: stops at an IE whose Length runs past its scope
column4: takes it, without the octets that it lacks
column7: An IE whose Length is greater than the octets of its scope has an invalid length; ie.UnmarshalBinary of go-pfcp returns no error for an IE header with nothing after it, whatever its Length

column4: reads the octets after the header, whatever the Message Length
column7: The Message Length gives the length of the message: ParseHeader of go-pfcp compares it with the octets after the header rather than after the first four, which no message matches, and takes every octet after the header as IEs of the message (§6.5 bundles messages in one datagram)

column3: stops at a Message Length that runs past the octets
column4: reads the octets after the header, whatever the Message Length
column7: A Request whose Message Length is inconsistent with its datagram is answered "Invalid length"; go-pfcp does not read the Message Length
A grouped IE type of a release after go-pfcp v0.0.24, whose last IE type is 271; go-pfcp keeps it as octets
CHID gives a CHOOSE ID after the address, which the value lacks; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
The Length of Flow Description of an SDF Filter runs past its octets; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
A Redirect Information whose lengths run past its octets, or whose Redirect Address Type is spare; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
The length of the Forwarding Policy Identifier runs past its octets; the accessor of go-pfcp returns the octets
DLPSI (bit 3) gives a DL Data Packets Size of two octets, which the value lacks; go-pfcp v0.0.24 does not have DLPSI
A Node ID of a spare Node ID Type: check() tells that it cannot be read, go-pfcp refuses its value
A Node ID value shorter than its type: check() tells it, go-pfcp refuses its value
The Node Address of an FQ-CSID lacks octets of its Node-ID Type; the accessor of go-pfcp returns the octets
A Volume Measurement of no flag: check() tells "no bit is set", go-pfcp refuses its value
A flag of a Dropped DL Traffic Threshold gives a field of eight octets that the value lacks; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
C-TAG and S-TAG are bits 5/7 and 5/8 of the Outer Header Creation Description: go-pfcp takes them from bits 6/7 and 6/8, and looks for a C-TAG or an S-TAG that is not there
Bit 5/7 or 5/8 gives a C-TAG or an S-TAG that the value lacks; go-pfcp takes those flags from octet 6
The Length of Flow Description of a Flow Information runs past its octets; the accessor of go-pfcp returns the octets
A Packet Rate of no flag, where "At least one bit in Octet 5 shall be set": check() tells it, go-pfcp refuses its value
APRC gives the additional packet rates that the value lacks; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
A Rule ID value of another length than the ID of its Rule ID Type: check() tells it, go-pfcp refuses its value
The Base Time Interval has four octets, which the value lacks; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error
Table 8.1.2-1 has 116 Reserved; go-pfcp reads it as the User Plane IP Resource Information of Release 15
Table 8.1.2-1 has 116 Reserved; go-pfcp reads it as the User Plane IP Resource Information of Release 15
A Multiplier has 12 octets; go-pfcp returns the octets of any length
The Subsequent Time Quota has four octets, which the value lacks; the accessor of go-pfcp returns no error

The Number of MAC addresses, the addresses, and the C-TAG and the S-TAG after their lengths, as Figure 8.2.103-1 has them: go-pfcp reads one MAC address more than the number says (i <= n) and both lengths at one octet, and refuses its own vector
As the MAC Addresses Detected of §8.2.103: go-pfcp reads one MAC address more than the number says, and refuses its own vector
The UE IP address Pool Id Length has two octets (octets 5 to 6); go-pfcp writes it in one, and returns the octets
An Alternative SMF IP Address of no address: check() tells "neither V4 nor V6 is set", go-pfcp refuses its value
An IP Multicast Address of no flag: check() tells "none, or more than one, of V6, V4 and A is set", go-pfcp refuses its value
The Rate Control Status Validity Time is present where UL or DL is set: go-pfcp reads it in a Packet Rate Status of neither
The User Plane Node ID value has eight octets (Unsigned64); go-pfcp reads six, as the Bridge ID of an earlier release
The PMF ports come with a PMF IP address (V4 or V6); go-pfcp reads them in a PMF Address Information of neither
An IE type of a release after go-pfcp v0.0.24, whose last IE type is 271
A conditional IE is incorrect, which its receiver answers "Conditional IE incorrect" where it can verify it; message.Parse of go-pfcp leaves it to its user
A conditional IE whose condition holds is missing, which its receiver answers "Conditional IE missing"; message.Parse of go-pfcp leaves it to its user
An IE does not frame, which its receiver answers "Invalid length": go-pfcp takes an IE header with no octets after it, whatever its Length
A mandatory IE that does not decode as its value is incorrect, which its receiver answers "Mandatory IE incorrect"; message.Parse of go-pfcp does not read the values
A mandatory IE of the message is missing, which its receiver answers "Mandatory IE missing"; message.Parse of go-pfcp does not check the IEs of a table, and leaves it to its user
A value that its clause has as reserved is invalid, which its receiver answers "Mandatory IE incorrect"; message.Parse of go-pfcp does not read the values
A value breaks a rule of its clause, which its receiver answers "Mandatory IE incorrect"; message.Parse of go-pfcp does not read the values
